name: MC Shan
hook: A Queensbridge rapper's borough anthem accidentally started one of hip-hop's first great beefs.
blurb: Shawn Moltke, born in the Queensbridge housing projects in 1965, joined Marley Marl's Juice Crew and signed to Cold Chillin' Records. His 1986 single 'The Bridge', produced by Marl, told the story of how their crew started in Queensbridge. It was widely heard as claiming Queensbridge as hip-hop's birthplace, though the lyrics don't actually say that, a case of how people hear a record running ahead of what it says. The Bronx's KRS-One, hearing it that way, answered with 'South Bronx' and then 'The Bridge Is Over', still cited among the most effective diss records ever made, and started a rivalry, the Bridge Wars, that made KRS-One's name at Shan's expense. It is widely seen as the first well-documented rap rivalry between two parts of a city, nearly a decade before the East Coast against West Coast conflicts of the 1990s.

signatureTracks.title: The Bridge
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Produced by Marley Marl; the record that started the Bridge Wars with KRS-One.

signatureTracks.title: Kill That Noise
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The Juice Crew's answer to KRS-One's 'South Bronx', the next round of the Bridge Wars. Boogie Down Productions replied with 'The Bridge Is Over'.
